key_insight: Laminating tested sheets builds tiers from known-good layers, so yield does not compound as it does over 64 monolithic tiers. Worth keeping as a packaging option for I-01819.
killer_doubt: Volume is not a cost axis: $/GB equals per-sheet $/GB. ACF film is ~15-25 um thick, more than the 12.5 um sheet pitch, so 800 sheets/cm cannot be built.
decisive_experiment: Laminate 16 printed test foils with thin ACF and edge-plated buses. Measure contact yield per sheet edge and bus resistance and capacitance, then project to 100 sheets. Folds into I-01819's demo.
prior_art: Irvine Sensors and Vertical Circuits edge-wired die stacks; SAIL roll-to-roll TFTs (HP Labs); project Phase B N-38 panel-level tiers.

key_insight: An active-matrix display backplane is already a 1T1C DRAM refreshed at 60 Hz. SAIL-imprinted IGZO at ~100 nm on a web gives ~200 GB/m2, a ~$100M line and no EUV.
killer_doubt: SAIL is proven only near ~1 um. At 100 nm, resist steps must hold ~10 nm across a metre-wide web. At $100-200/m2, not $20-40, cost is $0.5-1/GB.
decisive_experiment: Imprint a 4-level SAIL mask on polyimide-on-glass to make a 64x64 IGZO 1T1C/2T0C array at 100-150 nm. Measure Ioff, Vt spread, cell yield and 85 C retention. Then run one roll-to-roll pass at 500 nm to map distortion failures.
prior_art: HP Labs SAIL roll-to-roll a-Si TFTs; a-IGZO SAIL TFTs (IEICE 2018) (via search snippet); Thin Film Electronics printed memory; PragmatIC IGZO FlexICs; project N-38.

key_insight: Head fabs pattern ~20 nm magnetic stacks at U.S. sites, a real non-DRAM magnetic toolset. Magnetic writes would clear the triage endurance wall.
killer_doubt: Up to 64 shifts per read require <~1e-12 misplacement per shift; no vertical array has shown it in ~20 years. Head fabs are loaded by nearline demand, not idle.
decisive_experiment: Electroplate 20 vertical 3 um Ni-Fe/Co wires in a head-fab test lot with a TMR reader at the base. Run 1e9 shift cycles and count displacement errors per shift against the 1e-12 target.
prior_art: IBM Parkin racetrack (2008 onward); cylindrical domain-wall wires; Everspin U.S. MRAM fab; project N-82 racetrack in the capacitor hole.

key_insight: A secure-element tester signs what it measured itself. Binding the certificate to a retention-error PUF, not the SPD serial, makes it uncopyable and enables reuse supply.
killer_doubt: SPD serials can be rewritten, so a certificate can move to a worse module. ITAD firms already sell tested DIMMs with warranty, so the premium may be <5%.
decisive_experiment: Build 10 FPGA kits ($30k). Fingerprint 1,000 used DIMMs by retention-failure map, re-identify them blind after 6 months and 85 C, and survey 20 brokers on the price premium for signed versus vendor-tested modules.
prior_art: CST and ITAD DIMM testers; MemTest86 Pro reports; Iron Mountain/ITRenew recertified hyperscale hardware; DRAM retention and latency PUFs (Keller 2014; Kim, HPCA 2018).

key_insight: Pricing memory savings by installed base is a clean metric for demand reduction, and it costs nothing in wafers.
killer_doubt: Devices ship in fixed 8/12/16 GB steps, so a 10% RSS cut crosses no step and bits bought fall ~0%. Per-MB bounties are gameable via lazy allocation.
decisive_experiment: Using 2024-26 telemetry, regress OEM DRAM configs on Chrome and Electron RSS changes such as Memory Saver ($50k). If a 10% RSS drop moves no SKU mix, stop.
prior_art: Chrome Memory Saver and PartitionAlloc, Edge sleeping tabs, Electron memory work; Gitcoin and bug-bounty funds.

key_insight: Secure multiparty computation lets rivals publish only aggregate channel inventory, like JODI for oil, to deflate phantom double orders that amplify a ~10-15% gap into a 4x price.
killer_doubt: Three makers hold ~90% of bits and profit from opacity in a shortage; one abstention blinds the index. DOJ withdrew information-exchange safety zones in 2023.
decisive_experiment: Use an open MPC library with 5 distributors/ODMs and 3 buyers for 6 months ($400k). Test whether the weekly aggregate index leads contract-price moves better than TrendForce estimates.
prior_art: JODI oil data; WSTS aggregates; TrendForce/DRAMeXchange estimates; Boston Women's Workforce Council MPC payroll study; Atallah's secure supply-chain protocols.

key_insight: A free bootable test image removes the ATE cost for used-DIMM grading; a useful on-ramp to the signed-tester scheme in I-08260.
killer_doubt: The seller controls the host, so a signature from host software attests nothing. SPD serials can be cloned. This is a weaker duplicate of I-08260.
decisive_experiment: Red-team it: give 5 testers the image and ask them to forge a passing certificate for a failing DIMM by editing SPD or using a VM ($50k). If anyone succeeds, merge into I-08260's hardware-rooted version.
prior_art: MemTest86 Pro reports; TPM remote attestation; ITAD recertification; in-batch duplicate I-08260.

key_insight: Many fine-tunes over one resident base is the right shape for serving personalized models, and it cuts per-user HBM.
killer_doubt: BitDelta (2024) published exactly this. A 1-bit delta is still 1/16 of the base (6.25%), while a rank-16 LoRA on 70B is ~0.1-0.3%, so adapters already win by ~20-60x.
decisive_experiment: None needed. Benchmark BitDelta against S-LoRA quality per byte on 3 personalization tasks in a week of GPU time if a dossier wants the number.
prior_art: BitDelta (Liu et al., 2024) 1-bit sign deltas with fused multi-tenant kernels; S-LoRA and Punica serve thousands of adapters on one base.

key_insight: Making precision follow token age and attention mass matches how attention decays. Duplicate of I-04883/I-00304, which earlier batches dropped.
killer_doubt: Production KV already ships as FP8/NVFP4 (~4.5 bits with scales), so a 3-4 bit average buys ~1.2-1.5x, not 4-5x. INT2 erodes long-range retrieval.
decisive_experiment: RULER/needle test at 128k on a 70B model: compare the age-graded ladder against flat NVFP4 KV at equal bytes in ~1 GPU-week. Stop below 1.5x.
prior_art: KIVI, MiKV, ZipCache, KVQuant, PM-KVQ; NVFP4/FP8 KV caches in vLLM and on Blackwell.

key_insight: Re-creatable app state is kilobytes while warm heaps are hundreds of MB. OS-enforced semantic snapshots would trade heap residency for relaunch work.
killer_doubt: Android saved-instance state and low-memory-killer already do this. Phone DRAM growth is now driven by on-device models (a 3B INT4 model is ~2 GB resident), not warm apps.
decisive_experiment: Trace 20 top Android apps under 2 MB background caps and measure relaunch latency against warm resume ($100k). Compare the freed GB with the resident size of on-device AI models.
prior_art: Android onSaveInstanceState/SavedStateHandle and LMK, iOS state restoration, Marvin (USENIX ATC 2020) mobile memory management.

key_insight: Typed, opt-in lossy allocation keeps exactness the default while letting a controller trade error bounds for capacity on tolerant buffers.
killer_doubt: The big tolerant data is already compressed in software: AI tensors at 4-8 bits, media as JPEG/HEVC. Controller ZFP adds <=1.5x on the remainder, plus variable-size page management costs.
decisive_experiment: Capture heap dumps from 5 ML and media servers. Apply ZFP at each app's tolerance to the data that is not already quantized or compressed, and report the net capacity gain ($50k). Stop below 1.3x.
prior_art: EnerJ approximate types; Flikker; Doppelganger approximate cache (MICRO 2015); AVR approximate value reconstruction (Eldstal-Ahrens and Sourdis); CXL compression expanders.

key_insight: Attention is bandwidth-bound: an A100 scans 80 GB in ~40 ms (one decode step) at ~200 W per TB/s, like H100. Retired HBM beats CXL DDR as a KV tier.
killer_doubt: In a 2026 compute shortage, A100/H100s still rent and are not stranded. The 80 serial per-layer round trips (~10-20 us each) add ~1-1.6 ms per token unless pipelined.
decisive_experiment: Pair 4 A100-80GB with 1 H100 over 400G RDMA (~$150k used or rented), run Lamina-style offload at 128k context, and measure tokens/s/$ and TTFT. Then size the retirable A100/H100 HBM pool from fleet data.
prior_art: Lamina (Tsinghua 2024) offloads attention to consumer RTX 3090s (via search snippet); MegaScale-Infer and StepFun attention-FFN disaggregation. Retired datacenter GPUs as the tier: none found.
